## Turn 2: Create the cleanup script

```bash
cat > /workspace/docker_cleanup.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Docker cleanup script - uses environment variables for configuration

set -e

# Load config if not already loaded
if [ -f /workspace/docker_config.env ]; then
    set -a
    source /workspace/docker_config.env
    set +a
fi

LOG_FILE="${LOG_FILE:-/var/log/docker_cleanup.log}"

log() {
    echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $1" | tee -a "$LOG_FILE"
}

log "Starting Docker cleanup..."

# Cleanup stopped containers
if [ "${CLEAN_CONTAINERS:-true}" = "true" ]; then
    log "Removing stopped containers older than ${CONTAINER_AGE:-24h}..."
    docker container prune -f --filter "until=${CONTAINER_AGE:-24h}"
fi

# Cleanup unused images
if [ "${CLEAN_IMAGES:-true}" = "true" ]; then
    log "Removing unused images older than ${IMAGE_AGE:-168h}..."
    docker image prune -af --filter "until=${IMAGE_AGE:-168h}"
fi

# Cleanup unused volumes
if [ "${CLEAN_VOLUMES:-false}" = "true" ]; then
    log "Removing unused volumes..."
    docker volume prune -f
fi

# Cleanup unused networks
if [ "${CLEAN_NETWORKS:-true}" = "true" ]; then
    log "Removing unused networks..."
    docker network prune -f --filter "until=${NETWORK_AGE:-24h}"
fi

# Cleanup build cache
if [ "${CLEAN_BUILD_CACHE:-true}" = "true" ]; then
    log "Removing build cache older than ${BUILD_CACHE_AGE:-168h}..."
    docker builder prune -af --filter "until=${BUILD_CACHE_AGE:-168h}"
fi

log "Docker cleanup completed."
EOF
